events.title: Windows Security Event 4769 — A Kerberos service ticket was requested
aliases: A Kerberos service ticket was requested
events.source_locator: 4769(S, F): A Kerberos service ticket was requested

overview.summary: Records a Kerberos Ticket Granting Service (TGS) service-ticket request on a domain controller, including requesting account, target service, network origin, result and ticket cryptography plus Version 2 encryption-capability and request/response-ticket hash context.

event_versions.generation: Windows Server 2008 and later legacy shape
event_versions.notes: Legacy Event 4769 structure with account, service, network, ticket options/encryption, result, Logon GUID and transited-services fields.

event_versions.generation: Windows Server 2016 and later after January 14, 2025 or later Security Cumulative Update
event_versions.notes: Updated Event 4769 adds request/response ticket hashes plus account/service/domain-controller encryption capability, client-advertised etype and session-key encryption fields.

requirements: Audit Kerberos Service Ticket Operations success/failure auditing must be enabled on domain controllers where this telemetry is required.
Collection and normalization must preserve Event.Version because Version 2 contains security-relevant cryptographic capability and ticket-hash fields absent from the legacy Version 0 event.
collection.interpretation_note: Event 4769 is high-volume domain-controller Kerberos service-ticket telemetry. Failure Code 0x0 represents successful ticket issuance; non-zero values represent failures. Microsoft notes that 0x20 ticket-expiration failures are commonly informational, so result code, account, service, client and encryption context must be evaluated together.
collection.scope_note: Microsoft documents Event 4769 as generated only on Active Directory domain controllers.

correlations.purpose: follow Kerberos TGT issuance into subsequent service-ticket requests
correlate service-ticket activity with the resulting logon session on the accessed system when the GUID is populated
pivot to explicit-credential or special-group logon context when those events contain the same GUID
corroborate access to the requested Kerberos service with endpoint/network observations
place repeated failed service-ticket activity in broader account/authentication context

analysis: Investigate service tickets using DES or RC4 where account, service, domain-controller and client capability context indicates AES should normally be available; distinguish compatibility requirements from an actual downgrade.

Prioritize unusual or bursty requests for high-value service principals, uncommon Service Name values and anomalous client origins; repeated service-ticket requests can support Kerberoasting hypotheses only when surrounding identity and service context also aligns.
Use Logon GUID to pivot to 4624, 4648 and 4964 when populated, while treating an all-zero or absent GUID as a correlation limitation rather than missing proof.

Treat Version 0 and Version 2 separately in analytics: absence of Version 2 capability/hash fields on a legacy event is not missing telemetry, and common 0x20 ticket-expiration failures should not be elevated without additional evidence.

result_code.meaning: KDC_ERR_NONE — service-ticket request completed without an error.
KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN — client principal/account was not found in the Kerberos database.
KDC_ERR_S_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN — requested server/service principal was not found.
KDC_ERR_POLICY — request was rejected by KDC policy.
KDC_ERR_BADOPTION — KDC cannot accommodate the requested option.
KDC_ERR_ETYPE_NOTSUPP — requested encryption type is not supported.
KDC_ERR_CLIENT_REVOKED — client credentials are revoked or otherwise restricted.
KDC_ERR_SERVICE_REVOKED — credentials for the requested service are revoked.
KDC_ERR_KEY_EXPIRED — password/key is expired.
KRB_AP_ERR_TKT_EXPIRED — presented ticket has expired; Microsoft notes this is commonly informational.
KRB_AP_ERR_TKT_NYV — ticket is not yet valid.
KRB_AP_ERR_REPEAT — replay was detected.
KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW — clock skew is too great.
KRB_AP_ERR_MODIFIED — message integrity/checksum did not match.

events.title: Windows Security Event 4771 — Kerberos pre-authentication failed
events.source_locator: 4771(F): Kerberos pre-authentication failed

overview.summary: Records a Kerberos Ticket Granting Ticket pre-authentication failure on a domain controller, preserving the target account, krbtgt service, client network origin, ticket options, failure code, pre-authentication type and certificate-related fields.

event_versions.generation: Windows Server 2008 and later documented generations
event_versions.notes: Documented Event 4771 structure for Kerberos TGT pre-authentication failure.

requirements: Audit Kerberos Authentication Service failure auditing must be enabled on domain controllers where this telemetry is required.
Collection should preserve related Kerberos, account-lockout and endpoint/network telemetry so account, client address and time pivots can be correlated.
collection.interpretation_note: Event 4771 is domain-controller Kerberos failure telemetry. It can result from mistyped or stale passwords, expired or revoked credentials, clock or certificate problems, unsupported encryption/pre-authentication types, or hostile authentication attempts. Investigate the failure code, account, client address and surrounding authentication sequence before attributing intent. The certificate issuer, serial-number and thumbprint fields are schema-visible but documented by Microsoft as empty for Event 4771.
collection.scope_note: Microsoft documents Event 4771 as generated only on domain controllers and not generated for accounts configured to skip Kerberos pre-authentication.

correlations.purpose: compare failed pre-authentication with nearby TGT request activity and eventual Kerberos success/failure
correlate broader Windows failed-logon telemetry where the same authentication attempt also produces a logon failure
determine whether repeated Kerberos failures culminate in an account lockout
identify the process, service, scheduled task, VPN client or stored-credential source generating repeated Kerberos failures
validate source host and Kerberos traffic toward the domain controller

analysis: Prioritize repeated 4771 failures against privileged, service or high-value accounts, especially when many client systems target one account or one client targets many accounts.

Failure code 0x18 strongly indicates invalid pre-authentication data and commonly corresponds to an incorrect password; distinguish password guessing from stale service, scheduled-task, mapped-drive, VPN or cached-credential behavior.
Use Client Address and Client Port to pivot to the originating host, then correlate endpoint process and service telemetry rather than assuming the domain controller generated the faulty credentials.

Treat codes such as client-revoked, key-expired, policy-rejected, clock-skew, certificate or unsupported-encryption failures according to their own semantics; 4771 is not a single-condition bad-password event.

failure_code.meaning: KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN — client principal was not found in the Kerberos database.
KDC_ERR_POLICY — the KDC rejected the request because of policy.
KDC_ERR_ETYPE_NOSUPP — the KDC does not support the requested encryption type.
KDC_ERR_PADATA_TYPE_NOSUPP — the KDC does not support the requested pre-authentication data type.
KDC_ERR_CLIENT_REVOKED — the client credentials are revoked or otherwise not currently usable.
KDC_ERR_KEY_EXPIRED — the account password/key has expired.
KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_FAILED — pre-authentication information was invalid; commonly caused by an incorrect password.
KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW — client and KDC clocks differ beyond the accepted Kerberos skew.
KRB_AP_ERR_MODIFIED — integrity validation indicates the message stream was modified or could not be validated.

pre_authentication_type.meaning: No Kerberos pre-authentication type was used.
PA-ETYPE-INFO — KDC information about encryption type requirements.
PA-PK-AS-REP_OLD — legacy PKINIT/smart-card related pre-authentication response type.
PA-ETYPE-INFO2 — KDC encryption-type information used during pre-authentication negotiation.
PA-SVR-REFERRAL-INFO — server referral information in Kerberos pre-authentication data.

Network address of the client from which the TGT request reached the domain controller.
Source port of the client network connection used for the TGT request; zero can occur for local requests.

Kerberos error code explaining why the pre-authentication/TGT operation failed.

events.title: Sysmon Event 29 — FileExecutableDetected
events.source_locator: Events > Event ID 29: FileExecutableDetected

overview.summary: Records detection of creation of a new executable PE file, preserving process, user, target path, and hash context for investigation.
security_value: identify newly created PE executable files observed by Sysmon
attribute executable-file creation to a process and security principal
pivot from target path and hashes to related file and process evidence
distinguish detection telemetry from a maliciousness or prevention verdict

requirements: Sysmon must be installed and running.
The active Sysmon EventFiltering configuration must preserve FileExecutableDetected activity required by the investigation.
collection.configuration_note: FileExecutableDetected records detection of new PE executable-file creation. Filtering should be governed to retain required paths, processes, or investigation contexts.
collection.interpretation_note: Executable-file creation is common during legitimate installation, update, build, administrative, and application activity. Event 29 is observation telemetry and should be interpreted with process, user, path, hash, and surrounding evidence.

correlations.purpose: resolve process creation, command line, parent and user context for the process associated with the detected executable creation
correlate general file-creation evidence for the same target path
compare executable-file detection with executable-creation prevention evidence when both policies are deployed

analysis: Prioritize executable creation in user-writable, temporary, download, startup, service, or other security-sensitive paths when the responsible process is unexpected.
Correlate ProcessGuid, image, target path, hashes, signer or reputation context, parent process, and command line before assigning security meaning.
Treat Event 29 as executable-file detection evidence, not proof of malware or actor intent by itself.

fields.correlation: Use with ProcessGuid and time because PID values can be reused.

events.title: Sysmon Event 255 — Error
events.source_locator: Events > Event ID 255: Error

overview.summary: Reports internal Sysmon errors or conditions that prevented expected work, including heavy-load, implementation, security, or integrity-related failures.
security_value: identify Sysmon health or execution failures that can reduce expected telemetry
preserve the internal error identifier and description for operational diagnosis
correlate collection gaps with Sysmon service and configuration state
distinguish sensor-health evidence from a malicious verdict about activity on the host

requirements: Sysmon must be installed and running sufficiently to emit Operational-channel health or error telemetry.
collection.configuration_note: Event 255 is an internal Sysmon error/health event and has no normal EventFiltering configuration tag. Do not invent a filtering tag for this event.
collection.interpretation_note: An Event 255 record indicates a Sysmon error or condition that prevented expected work. Investigate repeated or security-relevant failures because they may create telemetry gaps, while avoiding unsupported assumptions about malicious intent.

correlations.purpose: correlate internal errors with Sysmon service state changes
correlate internal errors with Sysmon configuration changes
identify collection gaps or degraded telemetry around the reported error

analysis: Prioritize repeated Event 255 records, errors coincident with telemetry loss, service instability, configuration changes, or resource pressure.
Use the error ID and Description together with host resource, service, and configuration evidence to determine operational impact.
Treat Event 255 as sensor-health and execution evidence; investigate possible interference when supported by corroborating telemetry rather than inferring maliciousness from the error alone.

fields.meaning: UTC timestamp recorded for the Sysmon internal error.
Sysmon-reported internal error identifier or code used to distinguish the failure condition.
Human-readable Sysmon description of the internal error or condition that prevented expected work.
